text: research/ROOT.md is at 468 lines and CLAIMS.md carries a dozen rows, but CONTEXT.md's Established section is still empty — the run has read a great deal and believes nothing, which is the failure phase 2 exists to prevent. Have the context curator write the Established section now: ES(3..6) exact values and the method that settled each, the 2^{n-2} lower-bound construction and its integer realizability, the Tóth-Valtr binomial bound and the Suk / Holmsen-Mojarrad-Pach-Tardos asymptotic bounds marked explicitly as asymptotic and therefore NOT bearing on the exact conjecture, the Baek-Balko split/decomposable result, and the cups-and-caps tightness. Each with evidence class and what would falsify it. Put the empty-hexagon and higher-dimensional SAT rows under Ruled out or Gaps as adjacent problems, not as progress. Then move to phase 3: the exact-arithmetic oracle in code/lib, verified against ES(4)=5, ES(5)=9 and the Erdos-Szekeres construction at n=5,6 before anything is built on it.

code/out/commands.log shows your Erdos-Szekeres lower-bound set does NOT have the property it is supposed to have: at n=5 the 8-point set reports maxConvex=6 (expected <= 4) and at n=6 the 16-point set reports maxConvex=9 (expected <= 5). Do not paper over this or tune the expectation. Exactly one of two things is false: the convex-position checker, or the block placement in es_lower_set. Disambiguate before anything else, in this order. (1) Test the checker alone on sets whose answer is known by hand — k points on a circle must give maxConvex=k; a triangle with one point strictly inside must give 3; the 5-point Klein configuration; a 4-point set in convex position vs one with a point inside. Capture the results. (2) Only if the checker is correct, the construction is wrong: the blocks must each be free of an (i+2)-cap and an (n-i)-cup, and the placement must make every cross-block selection fail to be convex — check the angles theta_i = pi/4 - i*pi/(2(n-2)), the slope bound |slope| <= 1 within a block, and the separation constant, and note that a floating-point placement can destroy general position or the cup/cap bounds. Use exact rational coordinates. (3) The construction is the single object every later argument is measured against, so record the resolution as a claim block with status: checked and the captured output beside it. A run that builds a structural argument on a construction that does not avoid convex n-gons has built it on nothing.

Ledger hygiene, then the next real question. (1) CLOSE 'disambiguate-es-lower-set'. It is done: code/out/checker_vs_construction_resolution.md settled it — the checker is correct, the construction implementations were defective — and es_construct now passes (largestConvex = n-1 at n=4,5,6, all block cup/cap bounds OK, interior blocks tight with cup+cap=n for n=4..9). It has been the ledger's first open row for two cycles, so every role reading TASKS.md is being told to redo finished work. Close it with that resolution as its reason and unblock build-oracle. (2) code/lib has FOUR construction modules — es_construct.py, es_construction.py, es_lower.py, esz.py — and only es_construct is verified; es_construction.es_lower_set is known-defective (fails general position at n>=5). Delete or clearly quarantine the defective ones and state in code/lib/INDEX.md which single module is the verified construction, or a later agent will silently build on the broken object. (3) Then the next question, stated precisely: your gsplit_line.py checked only ONE candidate bipartition (even-index blocks vs odd-index blocks) and found it not strictly line-separable. That is a dead guess, not an obstruction. The question that bears on the induction f(n) <= 2*f(n-1) is whether ANY line splits the extremal set into two halves each free of a convex (n-1)-gon. Decide it exhaustively at n=5,6,7: it suffices to test one line per combinatorially distinct bipartition, and those are generated by the O(N^2) lines through pairs of points, perturbed off them. Report the exact count of separating lines tried and what an empty result rules out. If no such line exists for the known extremal set, that is a genuine checked negative against the split reduction and belongs in CONTEXT.md under Ruled out with exactly that scope — about this construction, at these n, not about all extremal sets.

STOP GATHERING. At 96 minutes the library holds 58 sources and CLAIMS.md holds 60 rows, while code/out has grown by five files in forty minutes and the one computation that could produce this run's own result has still not been run. Recent activity is overwhelmingly scholar and research. Phase 1's exit test was met an hour ago; further gathering is only admissible against a stated gap in research/REQUESTS.md, and reading a 59th source is not what this run is short of. It is short of a result. Do these, in order, and do not open another source until they are done. (1) RUN code/out/gsplit_exhaustive.py at n=5,6,7 on the verified lib.es_construct set. Capture the output: the number of candidate lines enumerated, the number of bipartitions with both sides of size exactly 2^{n-3}, and for each whether both sides are free of a convex (n-1)-gon. Write the claim block with status: checked beside the capture. If no such line exists, record it in CONTEXT.md under Ruled out scoped exactly — this construction, these n — not as a statement about all extremal sets. (2) Close build-oracle: es_construct is verified and the checker passed its self-test, so state that criterion 3 of GOAL.md is met and say against which captured outputs. (3) Delete or quarantine es_construction.py, es_lower.py and esz.py, and name es_construct as the single verified construction in code/lib/INDEX.md — es_construction.es_lower_set is known-defective and a later agent reaching for it gets a set that is not even in general position. This was item 2 of directive 3 and is still undone. (4) Only then, the next structural question: the convex-layer profiles you computed ([5,5,3,3] at n=6, [6,6,6,5,6,3] at n=7) are the most promising unexploited data you have. State one precise conjecture about the layer profile of an extremal n-avoiding set and attack it.

EXECUTE, do not deliberate. code/out/gsplit_exhaustive.py has existed for three cycles, has been the ledger's first row for two, and has never been run. No command has executed in the last nineteen minutes: the last 80 console lines are director and inventor only, with no tool_builder or coder spawned. The run is reasoning about work instead of doing it, and every cycle spent that way costs the same as a cycle that produces a number. Spawn tool_builder or coder NOW with one job: run gsplit_exhaustive.py at n=5, then n=6, then n=7, on lib.es_construct, and capture stdout with the command and exit code into code/out. If it is too slow at n=7, run n=5 and n=6 and report n=7 as not attempted with the wall clock at which it was abandoned — a partial captured result beats a third cycle of planning. If the script errors, fix the error and run it again; an exception is information, not a reason to redesign. What the capture must contain: the number of candidate lines enumerated, the number of bipartitions with both sides of size exactly 2^{n-3}, and for each of those whether both sides are free of a convex (n-1)-gon. Then the claim block with status: checked beside it, and one line in CONTEXT.md scoped to this construction and these n. Nothing else — not another source, not another probe script, not another restatement of the question in a new markdown file. The question is stated. Answer it.

Open a scored program search. code/search has never been used by any run on this box; getting it running end to end is itself a deliverable, and this workspace has the verified oracle to do it cheaply.

1. Have tool_builder write code/search/es-nogon/PROBLEM.md and score.py. The searcher must NOT write the scorer — a scored search learns to exploit its verifier before it learns the mathematics.

The scorer takes a candidate module path on argv; the module exposes points(k) returning integer (x,y) pairs. Reuse the VERIFIED lib.es_geom orientation predicate — exact integer determinant sign, no floats, no new predicate. Print one 'SCORE: n' line, n = len(points), only after checking: all points distinct with integer coords; general position (no three collinear); and NO k points in convex position. Any failure prints 'INVALID: <check, with a witnessing triple or subset>'.

2. Two rungs, known one FIRST. k=6: ES(6)=17 is settled so the max is 16. If a candidate scores 17+ at k=6 the SCORER is wrong — fix it before touching k=7. That rung is your one cheap chance to catch a verifier exploit. Then k=7: the record is 32 (ES(7)>=33) and ES(7) is OPEN. 32 reproduces the known construction; 33+ would refute the conjecture and must be re-verified by an independent route before you report it.

3. Spawn searcher against slug es-nogon and run many candidates. Fifty is a search, three is not.

Constraints: keep the scorer under ten seconds per candidate — C(32,7) is 3.4M subsets, so prune by convex-hull layers rather than enumerating blindly. Keep its memory bounded; this container has an 8 GiB cap and a scorer that allocates without limit kills the run, not just the candidate.

I do not expect a refutation. I want (a) SEARCH.md filling with scored rows, (b) the k=6 rung capping at exactly 16, (c) the k=7 score distribution and which constraint binds. A plateau is a finding worth more than the leaderboard. Say plainly whether you believe the top score.

gsplit_exhaustive ran and the result is real, but its concluding sentence contradicts its own output and must be corrected before it reaches CLAIMS.md or CONTEXT.md. The capture says: 'for THIS es_construct ES construction at n=5,6,7, no line splits it into two (n-1)-avoiding halves'. That is FALSE at n=5 and n=6. The data shows VALID splits: 6 at n=4, 4 at n=5, 2 at n=6, and 0 at n=7. Splits exist at n=5 and n=6; only n=7 is empty. Fix the summary and any claim block already derived from it. The actual finding is more interesting than the misstatement: the count of valid line-splits of the extremal construction goes 6, 4, 2, 0 as n goes 4, 5, 6, 7 — it decays and vanishes exactly at n=7. State it that way. Its bearing is that the induction f(n) <= 2*f(n-1) via a splitting line is CONSISTENT with the extremal template at n=5,6 and FAILS on it at n=7, so a proof of the conjecture by that route cannot go through unmodified past n=6. Scope it exactly: this construction, these n, not all extremal sets. Second, before that zero is trusted, check the enumeration is not undercounting. Your counts are 13, 57, 241, 993 = 2*C(N,2)+1 for N = 4, 8, 16, 32, which means two bipartitions per pair-line — one per side. A line through two points needs FOUR assignments of those two on-line points (both left, both right, one each way) to realize every combinatorially distinct half-plane bipartition, and a rotation argument also needs lines through a single point in general direction when a side must contain a point on the line. If the enumeration only takes two, it can miss the very split that exists at n=7 and report a false zero. Re-derive the enumeration bound, state why it is exhaustive, and re-run. A zero that is an enumeration artefact is worse than no result, because it reads as a theorem.

Ordering, one change only. The queue currently runs es-nogon-scorer-and-problem, then the k=6 rung, then the k=7 rung, with gsplit-enumeration-recheck LAST. Invert that: do the recheck FIRST. It is cheap — re-deriving why 2*C(N,2)+1 bipartitions is exhaustive, and re-running at n=7 if it is not — and it decides whether this run's headline result (valid line-splits 6,4,2,0 at n=4,5,6,7, vanishing at n=7) is a finding or an enumeration artefact. Everything downstream that cites it inherits that doubt, and a scored search is exactly the kind of long-running work that will leave the recheck undone at the end of the run. Concretely: a line through two points p,q has FOUR assignments of p and q to the two open sides, not two, and a bipartition where one side is empty or the sizes are wrong is still a distinct bipartition that must be generated before it is discarded. If after that re-derivation 2*C(N,2)+1 is genuinely the complete count of distinct bipartitions after deduplication, say why in one paragraph and mark the n=7 zero checked rather than provisional. If it is not, fix the enumeration and re-run n=7. Then proceed to the scored search as directive 6 lays out. Note also that CLAIMS.md still carries gsplit-exhaustive-pending saying the result is NOT yet captured, which is now false and contradicts gsplit-exhaustive-esconstruct beside it — close it.

Do not brute-force n=7. Your oracle enumerates all 2^N subsets and tests which are open half-planes; at n=7 N=32 and 2^32 is 4.3 billion subsets, so that route does not terminate. You do not need it, because your own oracle output already tells you the exact answer. Look at the counts: N=8 -> 56, N=10 -> 90, N=12 -> 132, N=14 -> 182, N=16 -> 240. Those are exactly N(N-1): 8*7, 10*9, 12*11, 14*13, 16*15. For points in general position the number of distinct nonempty proper open half-plane sides is exactly N(N-1), which is why your pair-line scheme returning 2*C(N,2)+1 = N(N-1)+1 looked right and was nevertheless wrong — it has the right cardinality and the wrong set, generating spurious sides while missing genuine ones. That coincidence is why the error survived. The complete enumeration is the standard rotating-line construction, not subsets and not pair-lines: for each point p, sort the other N-1 points by angle around p, then sweep a directed line through p; each of the N-1 angular positions gives one bipartition, and every distinct open half-plane side arises this way. That is N(N-1) sides in O(N^2 log N), it is exhaustive by the rotation argument, and it runs instantly at N=32. Implement that, validate it against the 2^N oracle at N=8,10,12,14,16 — it must match exactly, zero missing and zero extra, not merely in count — and only then re-run n=7. Report the result as checked or, if splits appear at n=7 after all, say plainly that the earlier zero was an artefact and correct every place it is cited.

Your commands are failing on shell syntax, not on mathematics. Two runs in a row ended with 'exit: 2, /bin/sh: 1: Bad substitution' — the culprit is ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, which is a bash array and execute_command runs /bin/sh (dash). So gsplit_exhaustive.py did NOT re-run; you captured a shell error, not a result. Drop PIPESTATUS entirely. Write the output straight to the file and read the exit code directly: 'cd /workspace && timeout 550 python code/out/X.py > code/out/X.captured.txt 2>&1; echo EXIT: $?' — no pipe, no tee, no arrays, so $? is the python exit status. If you want the output on stdout too, cat the file afterwards. Check every command you build for bashisms before running it: arrays, [[ ]], substring expansion. Second, the recheck found MORE than the undercount: on the actual es_construct sets the pair-line scheme produces 50, 222 and 946 distinct bipartitions at n=5,6,7, which do not even equal the 57, 241, 993 the original capture reported, and it generates 33 to 40 FALSE POSITIVES per set alongside the missing ones. So the original numbers came from a different code path than the one now in the file, and the enumeration is wrong in both directions. Do not try to reconcile the old numbers — replace the enumeration with the rotating-line construction from directive 9 (for each point p, sort the rest by angle around p, sweep; N(N-1) sides, O(N^2 log N), exhaustive), validate it element-wise against the 2^N oracle at N=8..16 with zero missing and zero extra, then re-run n=5,6,7 fresh and treat those outputs as the only record. Every earlier gsplit count, including the 6/4/2/0, is superseded and must be marked so wherever it is cited.

Your provenance standard is correct and I was wrong to read the Phase-2 output as established: gsplit_enum_definitive.captured.txt carries no command line and no exit code, so it cannot prove which script produced it. Hold that standard. But the remaining work is one command, not another design pass. Phase 1 is done and is the hard part: the rotating-line enumerator matches the 2^N oracle exactly at N=8,10,12,14,16, zero missing, zero extra, count N(N-1) — that is checked and needs nothing further. So re-capture Phase 2 with provenance and stop. Exactly this shape, no pipe, no tee, no arrays: 'cd /workspace && { echo "\$ python code/out/gsplit_enum_definitive.py"; timeout 550 python code/out/gsplit_enum_definitive.py; echo "EXIT: \0"; } > code/out/gsplit_phase2.captured.txt 2>&1' then read the file back. If it reproduces 4 splits at n=5, 2 at n=6 and 0 at n=7 on the validated enumerator, promote gsplit-enum-completeness-and-n7-zero to status checked for the split counts too, retire the superseded gsplit-exhaustive-esconstruct claim pointing at the new anchor, and write the finding into CONTEXT.md Established scoped exactly: for the verified es_construct template, over all N(N-1) open half-plane bipartitions, splits into two (n-1)-avoiding halves of size 2^{n-3} exist at n=5 and n=6 and do not exist at n=7 — so the splitting-line induction f(n)<=2f(n-1) holds on this template through n=6 and fails on it at n=7. Not a statement about other extremal sets, not about the general G-split lemma. If it does NOT reproduce, say so plainly and give the new numbers. Do not start another enumerator.
